meta.title: Attention Is All You Need

source_paper.citation: Vaswani, A., Shazeer, N., Parmar, N., Uszkoreit, J., Jones, L., Gomez, A.N., Kaiser, L., Polosukhin, I. (2017). Attention Is All You Need. NIPS 2017. arXiv:1706.03762v7

meta.audience: graduate ML seminar, familiar with seq2seq basics

template.note: generated test fixture standing in for organizer template

problem.statement: Dominant sequence transduction models (RNN/LSTM encoder-decoder with attention) compute sequentially along symbol positions, blocking parallelization within a training sequence and making training slow.

evidence.quote: Recurrent models typically factor computation along the symbol positions of the input and output sequences.
The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder.

method.statement: The Transformer: an encoder-decoder built solely on attention (multi-head self-attention + point-wise FFN), no recurrence or convolution, with positional encodings injecting order.

evidence.quote: Figure 1: The Transformer - model architecture.
The encoder is composed of a stack of N = 6 identical layers.
we use h = 8 parallel attention layers, or heads

results.statement: 28.4 BLEU on WMT14 EN-DE (over 2 BLEU above previous best including ensembles) and 41.8 BLEU on WMT14 EN-FR (new single-model SOTA) at a fraction of the training cost; also generalizes to English constituency parsing.

evidence.quote: The Transformer achieves better BLEU scores than previous state-of-the-art models on the English-to-German and English-to-French newstest2014 tests at a fraction of the training cost.
our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs

limitations.statement: The paper has no explicit limitations section. Inferred caveats: results shown on translation + one parsing task only; the fixed learned positional encoding targets sequences up to a maximum length; the paper does not study data efficiency below large corpora.

evidence.quote: We plan to extend the Transformer to problems involving input and output modalities other than text
evidence.note: future-work phrasing only; no limitations section exists in the paper

slides.claim: The Transformer removes recurrence and convolutions from sequence transduction using attention only.
slides.title: Attention Is All You Need
slides.subtitle: Vaswani et al., Google Brain / Google Research / U. Toronto — NIPS 2017 (arXiv:1706.03762) | lab seminar, 15 min

evidence.quote: We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.

slides.notes: One-line hook: this is the paper that made 'attention' the whole model instead of an add-on. Say the venue/year once, then move fast - the audience knows seq2seq. If asked later: authors span Google Brain and Google Research.

slides.claim: RNN-based transduction is fundamentally sequential, so training cannot be parallelized within a sequence.
slides.title: Problem: recurrence locks training into sequential steps

bullets.text: SOTA transduction = RNN/LSTM encoder-decoder + attention (2014-2016)
Hidden states ht computed one position at a time: ht = f(ht-1, xt)
Sequential dependency blocks intra-sequence parallelism; long training times
Attention already used to connect encoder and decoder - but only as a bolt-on

evidence.quote: Recurrent models typically factor computation along the symbol positions of the input and output sequences.
The fundamental constraint of sequential computation, however, remains.

slides.notes: Transition: 'everyone in this room has trained an LSTM and waited.' Emphasize the word 'intra-sequence' - GPUs are idle waiting for t-1. Anticipate the question 'what about convolutional models?' - mention ConvS2S appears later in the results table.

slides.claim: Core idea: keep only attention - self-attention replaces recurrence everywhere, at a fraction of the training cost.
slides.title: Core idea: attention only, no recurrence, no convolution

bullets.text: Self-attention relates all positions in a sequence to each other directly
Multi-head attention: h=8 parallel heads over d_model=512 (base)
Positional encodings inject word order (sinusoidal)
Trained in 3.5 days on 8 GPUs - a fraction of prior SOTA costs

evidence.quote: these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train
we use h = 8 parallel attention layers, or heads

slides.notes: This is the 'elevator pitch' slide - if the seminar only remembers one slide, make it this one. Stress that 'dispensing with recurrence entirely' was the heretical part in 2017. Do NOT derive Q/K/V here - next slide does architecture.

slides.claim: The architecture: 6-layer encoder (left) and decoder (right) built from multi-head self-attention + position-wise FFN sub-layers.

evidence.quote: Figure 1: The Transformer - model architecture.
evidence.note: architecture diagram, original figure from the paper

evidence.quote: The encoder is composed of a stack of N = 6 identical layers.

slides.notes: Walk the figure bottom-up on the encoder half first, then decoder. Point at the residual arrows while saying 'residual + LayerNorm around every sub-layer'. Q&A backup: exact FFN inner width is 2048 (Section 3.3).

slides.claim: Scaled dot-product attention is computed per head, then concatenated; complexity per layer is O(n^2 * d) but constant in path length.
slides.title: Inside a layer: scaled dot-product + multi-head attention

bullets.text: Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) V
Scaling by sqrt(d_k) keeps softmax gradients sane
8 heads of d_k=d_v=64 (base): different representation subspaces
Self-attention path length between any two tokens: O(1)

evidence.quote: We suspect that for large values of dk, the dot products grow large in magnitude, pushing the softmax function into regions where it has extremely small gradients
Multi-head attention allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions.
Maximum path lengths, per-layer complexity and minimum number of sequential operations

slides.notes: Write the formula on the slide but SAY only the intuition: 'every token asks every other token a question'. Contrast with RNN: path length between distant tokens drops from O(n) to O(1) - that is Table 1's punchline. If asked about quadratic cost: yes, O(n^2) in sequence length, acknowledged in Table 1 discussion.

slides.claim: Training recipe: Adam with warmup-then-decay schedule, heavy regularization (dropout 0.1, label smoothing 0.1).
slides.title: Training recipe (Sections 5.3-5.4)

bullets.text: Adam (beta1=0.9, beta2=0.98, eps=1e-9)
LR schedule: linear warmup (4000 steps) then inverse-sqrt decay
Residual dropout p=0.1; label smoothing 0.1
Base: 6 layers, d_model=512, 65M params; big: 213M

evidence.quote: We used the Adam optimizer [20] with β1 = 0.9, β2 = 0.98 and ε = 10−9.
